title: CFPB recorded response routes remain strongly product-shaped across 2024 and 2025
source_unit: published CFPB complaint record in a product-filtered API aggregation, grouped by calendar year received

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for date_received_min=2024-01-01 and date_received_max=2025-01-01; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Response shares are not remedy probabilities or customer harm rates; product issues, firm mix, and publication rules can differ.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2024; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher monetary-relief share than other products does not establish higher remedy adequacy or customer welfare.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2024; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Recorded non-monetary relief does not reveal whether a debt was corrected, reduced, or otherwise resolved for the consumer.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2024; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: An explanation label does not establish that a foreclosure, servicing, or payment problem was adequately resolved.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2024; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The explanation-dominant endpoint does not establish whether borrowers received correction, relief, or a workable repayment outcome.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2024; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Recorded response categories do not measure repossession avoidance, debt correction, transportation continuity, or customer exit.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for date_received_min=2025-01-01 and date_received_max=2026-01-01; response, timeliness, narrative, and in-progress buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, complaint propensity, and the added in-progress category remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase in explanation and decrease in relief labels do not establish lower remedy adequacy or a change in account-holder welfare.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2025; response, timeliness, narrative, and in-progress buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, complaint propensity, and the added in-progress category remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 2025 credit-card response mix cannot be interpreted as a remedy probability without account, issue, firm, and outcome denominators.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2025; response, timeliness, narrative, and in-progress buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, complaint propensity, and the added in-progress category remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 2025 response pattern does not reveal whether debt collectors corrected, reduced, or only explained the underlying issue.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2025; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The stable explanation-dominant pattern does not establish that mortgage servicing or foreclosure problems were adequately resolved.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2025; response, timeliness, narrative, and in-progress buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; the large untimely share may reflect product, servicing, routing, coding, or taxonomy changes and requires a field-definition review before causal interpretation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high untimely-response share is an institutional timing signal, not proof of borrower harm, delayed relief, or failed repayment outcomes.

observations.method: Product-filtered official CFPB API aggregation for calendar 2025; response, timeliness, and narrative buckets divided by the product-filtered published-record total.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product taxonomy, company coding, and complaint propensity remain relevant uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Recorded response categories do not measure repossession avoidance, debt correction, transportation continuity, or customer exit.

boundary: These are product-filtered trends in published CFPB complaint-system records, not representative customer samples, account-denominated harm rates, verified remedy rates, or causal estimates. Product and issue mix, complaint propensity, publication, routing, firm coding, and the 2025 in-progress/timeliness taxonomy can change the observed shares.
